source_file: tests/fixtures/schemas/opencode-config.schema.json -- OpenCode's own published JSON Schema, https://opencode.ai/config.json, vendored so the suite never needs the network
note: The one row in the set whose application publishes a machine-readable schema, so the rule *is* the schema and this file only says where MCC's block sits inside it and what the schema cannot express.
embed_evidence: the desktop card merges into the user's own ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json under provider.<id>, so what has to validate is the whole document with MCC's block in place -- not the block alone, which no schema describes.

credential.evidence: ProviderConfig.options.apiKey is a plain string in the schema, and createOpenAICompatible sends it verbatim as Authorization: Bearer. MCC used to write {env:MCC_AUTH_TOKEN}; OpenCode does expand {env:...}, but nothing sets that variable, so what went on the wire was the literal reference -- HTTP 401, measured against a scratch MCC server.

base_url_evidence: createOpenAICompatible builds new URL(baseURL + '/chat/completions'), and the trailing slash is stripped for you.
options_headers_evidence: ProviderConfig.options declares no 'headers'; the only two 'headers' properties in the whole schema belong to MCP server entries. The block validated with one anyway because options omits additionalProperties: false, so OpenCode dropped MCC's attribution header silently. Removed in 6.83.0 -- this rule is what stops it coming back.
top_level_unknown_key_evidence: the config validator throws ConfigInvalidError on an unknown key at the document root and opencode refuses to start, while an unknown key nested inside provider.<id> or a model is silently ignored (decodeUnknownExit with no onExcessProperty). The desktop path is safe because the models node is taken verbatim and MCC's _mcc_defaulted record never leaves the serialiser's root.
